questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to visit a country I hadn't seen already and go somewhere with beautiful nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough, just required asking around amongst the other students and the erasmus network

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had signed up for a buddy, which was helpful as I could text them regarding practical questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a bit unorganized when it came to the departments, they did not necessarily know that you were arriving.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just a facebook page, and it went pretty okay. Contact someone who has gone before you, they'll have contnact for a landlord, as that'll be cheaper than airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nicer to live off campus in the city, has that's where you'll be spending most of your time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to signup on a specific web page. However, to choose specific departments you had to write an email to the erasmus coordinator, who didn't reply to any emails for a month or two making the process a bit frustrating. I recommend if you get stuck in the process just to call them, as that makes everything go much faster.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email or call the erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My email with wishes for departments was not received. However, later I manage to arrange to change departments myself.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Think about which departments you are interested in - even when you are already in Crete, you can try to email the relevant doctors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In Crete the rotation is much less hands-on than in Denmark, you are mostly just watching the doctors do their job, and then most of the time they'll be doing it in Greek...

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Especially as an erasmus students the expectations of you are very very low. If you find the right doctor they'll teach you procedure like taking a blood gas or doing a urinary catheter, but you most likely won't be examining any patients on your own whatsoever.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In UCPH it is much more learning by doing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 5 weeks in internal medicine (internal medicine and infectious diseases) and 5 weeks in surgery (general surgery, thoracic surgery, neurosurgery)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend going to the neurosurgery department as the doctors there are passionate about teaching and there are few students. General surgery there are waaaay to many students and not a good teaching environment.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a Greek simcard as you can only use your Danish number for a certain amount of time abroad.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than expected. But renting a car is only 20-30 euro and then you can go on loads of adventures!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's lots of activities and a few hiking groups!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of hikes from different student organisations, but the erasmus network also arranged everything from wine tasting to yoga on the beach.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking!! The island is absolutely beautiful and you get to talk with the local students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and drive around the island or get a ferry to some of the small islands around - you get 50% discount on the ferries!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mostly it was difficult adjusting to the hospital, as the culture in regards to teaching was so different

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The greek students are all very open, make sure to talk with them on your departments!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The hospital atmosphere.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very open!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) adjust your expectations academically - just learning another health care system is a valuable experience 2) explore as much as you can in the weekends, there's sooo much to see 3) eat loads of gyros

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The hospital atmosphere

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
